subject: RLUSD cross-chain supply, gross transfer volume, payment-quality and concentration
mission_relevance: Separate stablecoin infrastructure adoption from economically meaningful XRP demand and prevent raw transaction-count/transfer-volume leakage into the XRP prediction feature store.

current_supply.other_supported_chains: Small residual balances on OP Mainnet, Ink and Unichain.
current_supply.interpretation: Ethereum currently holds roughly 72% of tracked RLUSD supply and XRPL roughly 27.5%. Over 30 days the displayed Ethereum supply rose 47.62% while XRPL supply fell 27.90%. This is a provider snapshot, not issuer reserve accounting or proof of a direct bridge transfer.

october_transfer_volume.provider: Token Relations, November 6 2026 post, quoted by Coinpedia November 13
october_transfer_volume.original_post_access: HTTP 403 through public retrieval; quotation preserved in Coinpedia article.

turnover_calculation.provider: Coindoo calculation from Token Relations transfer totals and DefiLlama daily historical supply
turnover_calculation.caveat: Gross turnover measures repeated movement, not unique economic value, new capital, beneficial owners or payments for goods and services.

week_starting_2026_11_02.interpretation: Ethereum narrowly retook the weekly lead; the October monthly lead did not persist in the latest reported week.

payment_quality_and_concentration.provider: Bitquery direct XRP Ledger on-chain investigation
payment_quality_and_concentration.cluster_funding_pattern: 110 wallets received XRP and RLUSD from Binance-labelled proof-of-reserves wallets; collectors swept flows through a destination-tag deposit account back to a Binance-labelled wallet. Bitquery says the pattern fits one Binance customer; it does not attribute conduct to Binance itself.
payment_quality_and_concentration.cluster_shutdown: The 110-wallet cluster wound down between October 14 and October 16, coinciding with the October 15 Cross River announcement. Bitquery explicitly says the causal reason is unknown.
methodology_limits: Counts XRP Ledger Payment transactions between distinct accounts that delivered the genuine RLUSD issuer currency; trades, self-payments, escrows, account deletions and failed transactions are excluded.
The 110-wallet cluster is inferred from common collectors and funding; it is not a verified real-world identity.
The 14,600 payments at least one RLUSD are not all independently proven commercial payments.
Exchange/custodian omnibus and destination-tag wallets can legitimately concentrate large settlement flows.
Issuer mint/redemption and round-trip transfers inflate gross transfer volume without equivalent net capital movement.

bank_rail.capability: RLUSD integrated into Cross River Core Operating System; eligible fintech businesses can access USD/RLUSD through one API and use XRPL settlement alongside ACH, wires and real-time payment rails.

feature_engineering_implications: Do not use raw RLUSD payment count as an adoption feature without bot/dust classification.
Store gross transfer volume, net issuer supply change, mint/redemption, self/round-trip flows and bridge movements separately.
Track high-value payment count/value, unique sender/receiver counts, top-10 concentration, HHI, issuer share, exchange/custodian-labelled destinations and source confidence.
Separate XRPL RLUSD stock from gross XRPL RLUSD flow and from XRP spot demand.
Do not infer that RLUSD transfer volume creates proportional XRP purchases; XRP fee and reserve demand is a separate, measurable channel.
Treat Cross River integration as deployed infrastructure with limited-state availability, but actual throughput remains undisclosed.
competing_hypotheses: H1: XRPL is developing genuine high-value institutional RLUSD settlement, reflected in the October transfer-volume lead and Cross River integration.
H2: Gross transfer volume is materially amplified by issuer mint/redemption, exchange/custodian sweeps and round trips; the Bitquery concentration analysis supports this caution.

H3: October activity may be a temporary venue/custody flow rotation; November 2 weekly volume was essentially tied and DefiLlama's November 14 supply snapshot shows Ethereum holding about 72% while XRPL supply fell 27.9% over 30 days.
model_admission: NOT_ADMITTED: aggregator and on-chain research summaries are not byte-exact Barrot source receipts; the measurement windows, source definitions and independent lineage must be ingested and reconciled before feature use.
